html:
SMTO-FIL-0003 — A file or folder with that name already exists

GUID: 55fb9c77-a83b-4770-af31-301ce39bee6c
Slug: file-already-exists
Domain: FIL · Subsystem: files

What happened

  • SMTO was asked to create something new, but a file or folder with that name is already in that place. SMTO left the existing one as it was.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO to list the destination folder so you can see what is already there. The existing item may be one you want to keep, or a copy from an earlier step.
  2. Give SMTO a different name or folder for the new file. A free name means the existing item isn't touched at all.
  3. If you do want the existing file replaced, say so clearly, for example "overwrite the existing report.txt". SMTO only replaces an existing file when you ask it to.

What success looks like

  • The new item appears under the name you chose, or the existing file shows your updated content.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't delete the existing item to make room until you've checked what it holds.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A create-only file operation (write, mkdir, copy, move, patch or transfer) found its destination already occupied, through a pre-check, EEXIST/ERROR_FILE_EXISTS, or a no-replace publish.

What this means

  • An existence check or OS error found an occupied create-only destination, or a destination appeared before no-replace publication. File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.

Why this can happen

  • An existence check or OS error found an occupied create-only destination, or a destination appeared before no-replace publication.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the exact destination and requested create/overwrite mode; distinguish an expected existing item from a concurrent appearance.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the existing item at the destination path. Choose another destination, or re-issue with explicit replacement (overwrite=true, or write mode replace with expected_revision) if replacing is intended; check changed_paths for items already created by the same request.
  • Choose another destination or use the supported explicit update operation if replacement is intended.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended new name is free, or an explicitly authorized supported update validates the existing revision.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
